title: Case Study: Biomarker Stratification and Dysbiosis in Atopic Dermatitis
text: Atopic Dermatitis (AD) multifactorial inflammatory skin disease characterized epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune hyperactivation, cutaneous microbial dysbiosis. case study demonstrates complete multi-omics reporting workflow cliomicplot, integrating four biological dimensions: Host Transcriptomics: Differential expression analysis NCBI GEO GSE121212 comparing lesional AD healthy control skin. Host Genetics & Clinical Severity: Patient objective SCORAD severity stratified loss--function variants filaggrin (FLG) gene. Cutaneous Metagenomics: Differential microbial abundance across anatomical predilection sites (cheek, forehead, antecubital crease). Systems Biology Multi-Domain Coupling: Central microbial network linked biophysical barrier function (TEWL, stratum corneum hydration), clinical severity, micro-climate drivers.
code: library(cliomicplot) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) clitheme("nature")

what: Step 1: Host Transcriptomic Signature (NCBI GEO GSE121212)
title: Case Study: Biomarker Stratification and Dysbiosis in Atopic Dermatitis
text: load bundled NCBI GEO GSE121212 RNA-seq dataset (geo_dermatology_series_de.rds), containing differential expression statistics 27 lesional AD, 28 psoriasis, 30 healthy control skin biopsies:
code: data_path <- system.file("extdata", "geo_dermatology_series_de.rds", package = "cliomicplot") series <- readRDS(data_path)  ad_labels <- c("SERPINB4", "CCL18", "S100A7", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G", "ALOX15", "GPLD1", "SPTLC3")  p_volc <- cliplot(   -log10(padj) ~ log2FC,   data = series$ad_vs_hc,   type = type_volcano(     fc_cutoff    = 1.5,     pval_cutoff  = 0.01,     point_size   = 1.8,     point_alpha  = 0.60,     label_genes  = ad_labels,     max_overlaps = 25   ),   preset = "nature",   title  = "Transcriptomic Signature: AD Lesional vs Healthy Skin (GSE121212)",   subtitle = "Bulk RNA-seq | FDR < 0.01, |log2FC| > 1.50" ) p_volc

what: Step 2: Clinical Severity Stratified by Host FLG Status
title: Case Study: Biomarker Stratification and Dysbiosis in Atopic Dermatitis
text: Loss--function variants filaggrin (FLG) represent strongest genetic risk factor AD. evaluate objective SCORAD across healthy controls, FLG wildtype AD, FLG mutant AD patients:
code: set.seed(42) cohort_df <- data.frame(   Subgroup = factor(     rep(c("Healthy Control", "AD (FLG Wildtype)", "AD (FLG Mutant)"), c(35, 45, 28)),     levels = c("Healthy Control", "AD (FLG Wildtype)", "AD (FLG Mutant)")   ),   SCORAD = c(     pmax(0, rnorm(35, mean = 3.5, sd = 2.0)),     pmax(5, rnorm(45, mean = 24.2, sd = 7.5)),     pmax(12, rnorm(28, mean = 38.6, sd = 9.2))   ) )  p_box <- cliplot(   SCORAD ~ Subgroup,   data      = cohort_df,   by        = "Subgroup",   type      = "boxplot",   palette   = "nature",   legend    = "none",   stat.test = "kruskal.test",   title     = "SCORAD Severity Stratified by Host FLG Genotype",   ylab      = "Objective SCORAD Index" ) p_box

what: Step 3: Cutaneous Dysbiosis Across Anatomical Sites
title: Case Study: Biomarker Stratification and Dysbiosis in Atopic Dermatitis
text: Using type_bubble_matrix(), evaluate differential bacterial abundance across three predilection sites (cheek, forehead, antecubital crease):
code: species <- c("S. aureus", "S. epidermidis", "S. hominis", "C. acnes", "M. restricta") sites   <- c("Cheek", "Forehead", "Antecubital")  da_ad <- expand.grid(Species = species, Comparison = sites, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) da_ad$log2FC <- c(   2.8, -1.9, -1.2, -1.8, 1.4,   2.1, -1.5, -0.8, -1.2, 0.9,   3.2, -2.4, -1.4, -2.1, 1.6 ) da_ad$qval <- c(   1.5e-5, 2.8e-3, 0.04, 3.1e-4, 0.02,   7.2e-4, 1.5e-3, 0.08, 1.2e-3, 0.05,   2.8e-6, 3.9e-4, 0.01, 9.8e-5, 0.007 )  p_bubble <- cliplot(   Species ~ Comparison,   data = da_ad,   type = type_bubble_matrix(     size_col = "qval",     fill_col = "log2FC",     min_size = 2.0,     max_size = 7.0,     palette  = "nature"   ),   title = "Cutaneous Dysbiosis Across Anatomic Sites",   subtitle = "Circle size = -log10(q-value); fill color = signed log2(Fold Change)" ) p_bubble

title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1 / anti-PD-L1) altered treatment paradigms solid tumors. Reporting results immunotherapy clinical trials requires integrating multiple endpoint modalities: Overall Survival (OS): Kaplan-Meier curves aligned numbers--risk landmark milestone rates (6 months, 1 year). Subgroup Consistency: Multivariable Cox proportional hazards forest plots stratified biomarker status (e.g. PD-L1 TPS). RECIST 1.1 Tumor Response: Waterfall plots displaying maximal target lesion shrinkage standard +20%+20\% −30%-30\% thresholds. Treatment Duration & Ongoing Response: Swimmer timelines indicating durable clinical responses active therapy database lock. Multi-Panel Trial Composite: 4-panel trial outcome figure assembled patchwork submission.
code: library(cliomicplot) library(survival) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) clitheme("nature")

what: Step 1: Overall Survival (Kaplan-Meier with Aligned Risk Table)
title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: Using NCCTG lung cancer clinical trial cohort (n=228n = 228), model overall survival comparing treatment cohorts, annotating landmark survival rates 180 365 days:
code: clitheme("nature")  p_km <- cliplot(   Surv(time, status) ~ sex,   data = lung,   type = type_km(     risk_table  = TRUE,     pval        = TRUE,     conf_int    = TRUE,     median_line = TRUE,     milestones  = c(180, 365)   ),   palette  = "nature",   title    = "Overall Survival",   subtitle = "Landmark Milestones at 6 & 12 Months",   ylab     = "Survival Probability" ) p_km

what: Step 2: Treatment Consistency Across PD-L1 Subgroups (Forest Plot)
title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: Evaluating consistency across biomarker subgroups (PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score: <1%<1\%, 1–49%1\text{--}49\%, ≥50%\ge 50\%):
code: io_subgroups <- data.frame(   Variable = c("Overall Intention-to-Treat", "PD-L1 TPS >= 50%", "PD-L1 TPS 1-49%", "PD-L1 TPS < 1%"),   HR       = c(0.68, 0.49, 0.72, 0.91),   CI_low   = c(0.55, 0.36, 0.54, 0.71),   CI_high  = c(0.84, 0.67, 0.96, 1.16),   P        = c(0.0004, 0.0001, 0.024, 0.420) )  clitheme("nature")  p_forest <- cliplot(   HR ~ Variable,   data = io_subgroups,   type = type_forest(     ref_line    = TRUE,     ref_val     = 1.0,     sort        = TRUE,     stripe      = TRUE,     show_values = TRUE   ),   title    = "Subgroup Consistency",   subtitle = "Hazard Ratios Across PD-L1 Strata" ) +   theme(legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 25, b = 4, l = 10, "pt")) p_forest

title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: Waterfall plots rank individual patients maximum percentage change target lesion sum diameters baseline:
code: set.seed(42) n_eval <- 24 pat_ids <- paste0("PT-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_eval)) changes <- sort(rnorm(n_eval, mean = -22, sd = 36), decreasing = TRUE)  wf_io <- data.frame(   Patient = factor(pat_ids, levels = pat_ids),   Change  = changes )  clitheme("nature")  p_wf <- cliplot(   Change ~ Patient,   data = wf_io,   type = type_waterfall(     show_labels         = FALSE,     response_thresholds = c("PD" = 20, "PR" = -30),     bar_width           = 0.72   ),   title    = "Tumor Burden Response",   subtitle = "RECIST 1.1 Criteria (PD: +20%, PR: -30%)" ) +   labs(     x = "Individual Patients (n = 24, ranked by change)",     y = "Best % Change in Target Lesions"   ) +   theme(     axis.text.x     = element_blank(),     axis.ticks.x    = element_blank(),     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.title    = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),     legend.text     = element_text(size = 6.5),     legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),     plot.margin     = margin(t = 6, r = 8, b = 4, l = 4, "pt")   )  p_wf

what: Step 4: Swimmer Plot of Treatment Duration
title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: Swimmer plots track patient timelines study. Arrowheads denote patients actively continuing therapy data cutoff:
code: set.seed(123) imtrial <- data.frame(   Patient  = factor(pat_ids, levels = pat_ids),   Duration = sort(runif(n_eval, 4, 32)),   BestResp = sample(c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD"), n_eval, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.15, 0.35, 0.30, 0.20)),   Ongoing  = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n_eval, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.55)) )  clitheme("nature")  p_swim <- cliplot(   Duration ~ Patient,   data = imtrial,   type = type_swimmer(     bar_fill      = "BestResp",     ongoing       = "Ongoing",     bar_linewidth = 2.6   ),   bar_palette = "jama",   title       = "Treatment Duration",   subtitle    = "Ongoing Response at Database Cutoff",   ylab        = "Months from Enrollment" ) +   labs(x = "Time on Study (months)", y = "Patients (n = 24)") +   theme(     axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 5.2),     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.title    = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),     legend.text     = element_text(size = 6.5),     legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),     plot.margin     = margin(t = 6, r = 8, b = 4, l = 4, "pt")   )  p_swim

title: Case Study: Immuno-Oncology Biomarkers and Trial Endpoints
text: assemble four endpoint figures publication composite using patchwork:
code: library(patchwork)  p_composite <- (p_km | p_forest) / (p_wf | p_swim) +   plot_layout(heights = c(1.0, 1.1)) +   plot_annotation(     tag_levels = "a",     tag_prefix = "(",     tag_suffix = ")"   )  p_composite

title: Getting Started with cliomicplot
text: cliomicplot unified grammar publication-ready clinical multi-omics figures built directly ggplot2. Designed around visual principles Nature, Cell, Science, offers: 55+ specialized plot types spanning clinical trials (Kaplan-Meier milestones, MCID dumbbells, trajectories, swimmers, waterfalls, forest plots), multi-omics (volcano, GSEA, UpSet, PCA, heatmaps), systems biology network architectures (concentric/bipolar cross-networks, 4-corner environmental coupling). 13 publication themes covering open-axis designs (nature, science, cell, nejm, lancet) full-box Elsevier/IEEE frames (scifig). 55+ curated color palettes strict color vision deficiency (CVD) accessibility. Publisher trim sizing (cli_journal_size()) 9 major publishers vector compliance checks (cli_save()).
code: library(cliomicplot) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)

title: Coupled Environmental Networks and Multi-Network Architectures
text: microbiome research, systems immunology, molecular ecology, evaluating community organization requires moving beyond isolated correlation matrices. cliomicplot provides integrated architecture : Cross-Condition Network Graphs (cliplot_cross_network_graph()): Visualizing multi-group modular topology across 8 journal-styled layouts (concentric, bipolar, science, ring, etc.). Coupled Environmental Networks (cliplot_env_network()): Coupling central microbial co-occurrence network 1 4 peripheral multi-domain environmental clinical correlation heatmaps. Layered Grammar Graphics: S3 grammar primitives (geom_env_boundary(), geom_env_central_network(), geom_env_corner_heatmaps(), geom_env_links(), coord_env_network()) enabling step--step layer composition. Statistical Cross-Network Validation: Hypergeometric module overlap (type_module_compare()), module-trait heatmaps (type_module_trait()), permutation null models (cli_network_permutation()), Mantel tests (cli_mantel()), targeted attack robustness (cli_network_robustness()).
code: library(cliomicplot) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) clitheme("nature")

title: Coupled Environmental Networks and Multi-Network Architectures
text: Co-occurrence networks constructed across disease states (e.g., Healthy Control vs. Lesional Disease) require spatial separation maintains readability highlighting shared vs. condition-specific edges. cliplot_cross_network_graph() provides topological layout algorithms designed publication figures:
code: demo_net <- generate_demo_cross_network()  p_node <- cliplot_cross_network_graph(   nodes       = demo_net$nodes,   edges       = demo_net$edges,   cross_edges = demo_net$cross_edges,   level       = "node",   style       = "bipolar",   preset      = "nature",   scifig      = TRUE,   title       = "Cross-Network Modular Architecture (Bipolar Layout)" ) +   labs(subtitle = "Separating Discovery (Left) and Replication (Right) Community Subgraphs") p_node

title: Coupled Environmental Networks and Multi-Network Architectures
text: cliomicplot supports four primary topological styles: style = "bipolar": Positions two condition networks opposing bilateral poles (e.g. left right hemispheres) inter-condition bridging links across center. style = "concentric": Positions core hub module inner circle peripheral satellite modules outer concentric ring. style = "science": Science-journal jewel styling high-contrast saturated nodes, darkened backgrounds, stroke-width weighting degree centrality. style = "ring": Equal-spaced modular clusters arranged along circular orbit.
code: p_concentric <- cliplot_cross_network_graph(   nodes       = demo_net$nodes,   edges       = demo_net$edges,   cross_edges = demo_net$cross_edges,   level       = "node",   style       = "concentric",   preset      = "science",   scifig      = TRUE,   title       = "Concentric Multi-Tier Modular Architecture" ) +   labs(subtitle = "Core Commensal Hubs (Inner) vs Satellite Pathobionts (Outer)") p_concentric

what: 3. Layered Grammar of Graphics for Coupled Networks
title: Coupled Environmental Networks and Multi-Network Architectures
text: cliomicplot provides layered grammar graphics coupled environmental networks: cli_env_network_data(): Constructor assembling nodes, edges, corner heatmaps, inter-domain links S3 data object. geom_env_boundary(): Boundary rings separating network modules. geom_env_central_network(): Circular co-occurrence network module arcs intra-module edges. geom_env_corner_heatmaps(): Peripheral multi-domain correlation heatmaps. geom_env_links(): Curvature-controlled connecting links collision pruning. coord_env_network(): Cartesian coordinate system fixed standard [−7.4,7.4][-7.4, 7.4] canvas. theme_env_network(): Zero-margin canvas theme eliminating axes grids.
code: # 1. Build environment network data object net_data <- cli_env_network_data(preset = "nature", compact = TRUE)  # 2. Layer-by-layer ggplot2 assembly p_layered <- ggplot() +   geom_env_boundary(data = net_data) +   geom_env_central_network(data = net_data) +   geom_env_corner_heatmaps(data = net_data) +   geom_env_links(data = net_data) +   coord_env_network() +   theme_env_network() +   labs(title = "Coupled Network Assembled via Grammar Layers")  p_layered

title: Coupled Environmental Networks and Multi-Network Architectures
text: validating networks across independent cohorts, type_module_compare() tests whether discrete modules identified discovery remain preserved validation cohorts:
code: set.seed(42) taxa_pool <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:120) net_discovery <- sample(c("M1_StaphCommensal", "M2_Lipophilic", "M3_Coryneform", "M4_PathogenCluster"), 120, replace = TRUE) net_replication <- net_discovery  # Reorganize 30% of taxa to simulate biological perturbation perm_idx <- sample(1:120, 36) net_replication[perm_idx] <- sample(c("ModA_Commensal", "ModB_LipidUtil", "ModC_Actinobacteria", "ModD_Inflammation"), 36, replace = TRUE) net_replication[-perm_idx] <- gsub("M1_StaphCommensal", "ModA_Commensal", net_replication[-perm_idx]) net_replication[-perm_idx] <- gsub("M2_Lipophilic", "ModB_LipidUtil", net_replication[-perm_idx]) net_replication[-perm_idx] <- gsub("M3_Coryneform", "ModC_Actinobacteria", net_replication[-perm_idx]) net_replication[-perm_idx] <- gsub("M4_PathogenCluster", "ModD_Inflammation", net_replication[-perm_idx])  network_df <- data.frame(   Taxon       = taxa_pool,   Discovery   = net_discovery,   Replication = net_replication,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  p_overlap <- cliplot(   Replication ~ Discovery,   data = network_df,   type = type_module_compare(     fill_by     = "rf",     show_stars  = TRUE,     show_totals = TRUE   ),   preset = "nature",   title  = "Cross-Network Module Preservation: Discovery vs Replication",   xlab   = "Discovery Cohort Modules",   ylab   = "Replication Cohort Modules" ) p_overlap

title: Nature/Cell/Science-Quality Figures with cliomicplot
text: Publishing premier scientific journals—Nature, Cell, Science (CNS)—demands strict visual, typographic, statistical discipline: Exact physical trim sizing: Figures must drawn publisher’s printed column widths (e.g., 89 mm single-column, 120 mm 1.5-column, 183 mm double-column) rather arbitrary canvas scaled typesetting. Minimalist typography data--ink ratio: -figure titles removed (figure explanations belong legend/caption); panel identifier tags (, b, c, d) sit upper left; font sizes constrained 5–7 pt final print scale. Open axes vs. full-box frames: Top right spines removed Nature Science (theme_cli_nature(), theme_cli_science()), structured spines outward ticks preserved Cell SCI/Elsevier styles (theme_cli_cell(), theme_cli_scifig()). Clinical biological integrity: Clinical figures prioritize effect magnitudes raw p-values (e.g. MCID thresholds), track exact denominators, report landmark milestones, present multi-omics evidence side--side. vignette demonstrates cliomicplot creates publication-ready figures matching exact journal requirements, drawing real proteomics, metabolomics, clinical datasets bundled package.
code: library(cliomicplot) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)  clipar(stat.test = NULL) # Disable auto statistical overlays for clean journal look # Helper to resolve bundled example datasets resolve_data = function(filename) {   pkg_path = system.file("extdata", filename, package = "cliomicplot")   if (pkg_path != "" && file.exists(pkg_path)) return(pkg_path)   fallback = file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback)) return(fallback)   fallback2 = file.path("inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback2)) return(fallback2)   stop("Cannot locate ", filename) }  # 1. AD/PD cortex proteomics (MaxQuant) e_adpd = new.env() load(resolve_data("ADPD_cortex_Maxquant.RData"), envir = e_adpd) adpd_meta = e_adpd$MetaData adpd_wide = e_adpd$data_wide adpd_res  = e_adpd$results_long adpd_long = e_adpd$data_long  # 2. Stroke brain time-course proteomics e_stroke = new.env() load(resolve_data("StrokeBrain_TimeCourse.RData"), envir = e_stroke) stroke_long = e_stroke$data_long stroke_meta = e_stroke$MetaData  # 3. Aging & High-Fat Caloric Diet metabolomics e_aging = new.env() load(resolve_data("AgingHFCD_Metabolomics.RData"), envir = e_aging) aging_meta = e_aging$MetaData aging_res  = e_aging$results_long

code: top10_ids = r_adctl$UniqueID[1:10] sub_long = adpd_long[adpd_long$UniqueID %in% top10_ids & adpd_long$group %in% c("CTL", "AD"), ] means = stats::aggregate(expr ~ UniqueID + group, data = sub_long, FUN = mean) wide  = stats::reshape(means, idvar = "UniqueID", timevar = "group", direction = "wide") names(wide) = c("protein", "CTL", "AD") wide$symbol = sub("_.*$", "", wide$protein)  slope_df = data.frame(   subject   = rep(wide$symbol, 2),   condition = factor(rep(c("Control", "Alzheimer"), each = nrow(wide)), levels = c("Control", "Alzheimer")),   abundance = c(wide$CTL, wide$AD) )  cliplot(abundance ~ condition, data = slope_df,         type = type_slope(pair = "subject"),         theme = "nature", palette = "npg",         xlab = "Cortex Condition",         ylab = "Mean Abundance (log2 LFQ)") +   labs(tag = "f") +   theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))

title: Microbial Metagenomics and mGWAS in Clinical Cohorts
text: Microbial GWAS maps bacterial genetic variation (single nucleotide variants indels) continuous clinical outcomes SCORAD treatment response. type_manhattan() draws chromosome positions significance cutoff lines labeled gene hits:
code: set.seed(42) mgwas_df <- data.frame(   pos  = seq(2000, 400000, by = 2500),   qval = runif(160, 0.02, 1.0),   gene = "",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Insert significant microbial variant associations hit_positions <- c(22, 68, 114, 142) mgwas_df$qval[hit_positions] <- c(3.2e-5, 8.4e-6, 4.1e-7, 1.9e-5) mgwas_df$gene[hit_positions] <- c("agrA", "mecA", "tsst-1", "ebpS")  cliplot(   qval ~ pos,   data = mgwas_df,   type = type_manhattan(     threshold  = 0.01,     label_col  = "gene",     point_size = 1.3,     xlab       = "Staphylococcus aureus Genome Position (bp)",     ylab       = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))   ),   title = "Microbial GWAS: Bacterial Variants Associated with Eczema Severity" )

title: Microbial Metagenomics and mGWAS in Clinical Cohorts
text: Bacterial vertical transmission strain persistence across early infancy evaluated across mother-infant dyads. type_sharing_heatmap() summarizes binary dyad sharing patterns across species:
code: set.seed(42) dyads <- paste0("Dyad ", sprintf("%02d", 1:14)) taxa <- c("S. epidermidis ST2", "S. epidermidis ST5", "S. hominis ST1",           "C. acnes IA", "C. acnes II", "M. restricta ST4")  dyad_data <- expand.grid(Taxon = taxa, Dyad = dyads, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) dyad_data$Transmission <- ifelse(   runif(nrow(dyad_data)) > 0.44, "Shared (Transmitted)", "Not shared" )  cliplot(   Taxon ~ Dyad,   data = dyad_data,   type = type_sharing_heatmap(     status_col     = "Transmission",     shared_label   = "Shared (Transmitted)",     shared_color   = "#E64B35",     unshared_color = "#EDF1F7",     legend_title   = "Dyad Status"   ),   title = "Mother-Infant Strain Transmission at 12 Months" )

text: Three real datasets bundled cliomicplot inst/extdata/:

# Resolve data paths (works for both installed package and devel/devtools::load_all) resolve_data = function(filename) {   pkg_path = system.file("extdata", filename, package = "cliomicplot")   if (pkg_path != "" && file.exists(pkg_path)) return(pkg_path)   # Fallback: look relative to the vignette source directory   fallback = file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback)) return(fallback)   # Fallback: direct path   fallback2 = file.path("inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback2)) return(fallback2)   stop("Cannot find data file: ", filename) }  adpd_path   = resolve_data("ADPD_cortex_Maxquant.RData") stroke_path = resolve_data("StrokeBrain_TimeCourse.RData") aging_path  = resolve_data("AgingHFCD_Metabolomics.RData")  load(adpd_path)   # → data_long, data_wide, results_long, MetaData, ProteinGeneName adpd = list(   long    = data_long,   wide    = data_wide,   results = results_long,   meta    = MetaData,   genes   = ProteinGeneName )  load(stroke_path)  # → data_long, data_wide, results_stat, MetaData, ProteinGeneName stroke = list(   long    = data_long,   wide    = data_wide,   results = results_stat,   meta    = MetaData,   genes   = ProteinGeneName )  load(aging_path)   # → data_long, data_wide, results_long, MetaData, ProteinGeneName aging = list(   long    = data_long,   wide    = data_wide,   results = results_long,   meta    = MetaData,   genes   = ProteinGeneName )  cat(sprintf("AD/PD proteomics : %d proteins × %d samples
", nrow(adpd$wide), ncol(adpd$wide))) #> AD/PD proteomics : 7163 proteins × 49 samples cat(sprintf("Stroke timecourse: %d proteins × %d samples
", nrow(stroke$wide), ncol(stroke$wide))) #> Stroke timecourse: 7565 proteins × 70 samples cat(sprintf("Aging metabolomics: %d metabolites × %d samples
", nrow(aging$wide), ncol(aging$wide))) #> Aging metabolomics: 393 metabolites × 590 samples

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: Principal component analysis AD/PD cortex proteomics data. Groups represent Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), combined AD+PD, controls:  axis labels include variance-explained percentages automatically. AD, PD, AD+PD groups show distinct separation controls along PC1.
code: # Build group labels and transpose for sample-level PCA adpd$meta$GroupLabel = adpd$meta$group adpd$wide_clean = adpd$wide adpd$wide_clean[is.na(adpd$wide_clean)] = 0  # For sample-level PCA: transpose to samples × proteins adpd$samples_mat = t(adpd$wide_clean)  clitheme("nature") #> Theme set to: nature cliplot(adpd$samples_mat,         type = type_pca(           pc_x          = 1,           pc_y          = 2,           center        = TRUE,           scale.        = TRUE,           add_ellipse   = TRUE,           ellipse_level = 0.95,           point_size    = 2.5         ),         by       = adpd$meta$GroupLabel,         palette  = "npg",         stat.test = NULL,         title    = "**Figure 1** — PCA of AD/PD Cortex Proteomics",         subtitle = sprintf("PC1 vs. PC2, %d samples × %d proteins, 95%% CI ellipses",                           ncol(adpd$wide), nrow(adpd$wide))) +   cli_markdown()

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: Volcano plot AD+PD vs. Control comparison AD/PD proteomics dataset. extract ADPDvsCTL test results table:  [!TIP] advanced volcano styling (asymmetric fold-change thresholds, gene-set callouts, multi-comparison small multiples), see dedicated Differential Expression Volcano Plots vignette.
code: # Filter to one comparison and prepare volcano data adpd_de = subset(adpd$results, test == "ADPDvsCTL") rownames(adpd_de) = adpd_de$UniqueID #> Warning: Setting row names on a tibble is deprecated. # Log-transform P-values adpd_de$negLogP = -log10(adpd_de$P.Value)  n_tested = nrow(adpd_de) n_de = sum(abs(adpd_de$logFC) > 0.5 & adpd_de$P.Value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) clitheme("cell") #> Theme set to: cell cliplot(negLogP ~ logFC, data = adpd_de,         type = type_volcano(           pval_cutoff  = 0.05,           fc_cutoff    = 0.5,           label_genes  = "significant",           max_overlaps = 20,           point_alpha  = 0.5         ),         title    = "**Figure 3** — Volcano Plot: AD+PD vs. Control",         subtitle = "AD/PD Cortex Proteomics | p < 0.05, |log<sub>2</sub>FC| > 0.5",         caption  = sprintf("%d proteins tested; %d significant",                            nrow(adpd_de),                            sum(abs(adpd_de$logFC) > 0.5 & adpd_de$P.Value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))) +   cli_markdown()

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: MA plot shows relationship fold-change mean expression, DE proteins highlighted:  LOESS trend line approximately flat around y = 0, indicating systematic intensity-dependent bias — good data quality.
code: # Compute mean expression from data_long for each protein adpd_means = aggregate(expr ~ UniqueID, data = adpd$long, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) names(adpd_means)[2] = "baseMean"  # Merge with DE results adpd_ma = merge(adpd_de, adpd_means, by = "UniqueID", all.x = TRUE) adpd_ma = adpd_ma[!is.na(adpd_ma$baseMean), ]  clitheme("science") #> Theme set to: science cliplot(logFC ~ baseMean, data = adpd_ma,         type = type_ma(           pval_cutoff = 0.05,           add_loess   = TRUE,           loess_color = "#3C5488",           sig_color   = "#E64B35",           ns_color    = "grey70",           point_size  = 1.2,           point_alpha = 0.4         ),         title    = "**Figure 4** — MA Plot: AD+PD vs. Control",         subtitle = "DE proteins highlighted (p < 0.05), LOESS trend") +   cli_markdown() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

text: Clustered heatmap top 40 differentially expressed proteins: Note: heatmap uses ComplexHeatmap. Install BiocManager::install("ComplexHeatmap").
code: # Get top 40 DE proteins by significance adpd_de_sorted = adpd_de[order(adpd_de$P.Value), ] top40_ids = head(adpd_de_sorted$UniqueID, 40)  # Build heatmap matrix hm_mat = as.matrix(adpd$wide_clean[top40_ids, ]) hm_mat = t(scale(t(hm_mat))) hm_mat[is.nan(hm_mat) | is.infinite(hm_mat)] = 0  # Column annotations ann_col = data.frame(   Group = adpd$meta$GroupLabel,   row.names = adpd$meta$sampleid ) # Build named color vector for annotation grp_levels = unique(ann_col$Group) grp_colors = c("#E64B35","#4DBBD5","#00A087","#3C5488","#E18727")[1:length(grp_levels)] names(grp_colors) = grp_levels ann_colors = list(Group = grp_colors)  cliplot(hm_mat,         type = type_heatmap(           scale             = "none",           cluster_rows      = TRUE,           cluster_cols      = TRUE,           annotation_col    = ann_col,           annotation_colors = ann_colors,           color_low         = "#2166AC",           color_mid         = "#F7F7F7",           color_high        = "#B2182B",           fontsize          = 9         )) +   ggplot2::labs(title = "**Figure 5** — Top 40 DE Proteins (Z-score)")

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: Time-course proteomics mouse stroke model. cluster protein expression trajectories across 5 time points (days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28 post-stroke):  panel shows one cluster individual protein trajectories (grey) cluster centroid (red). Clusters reveal distinct response patterns: acute responders (D1 peak), late responders (D14–D28), sustained changes.
code: # Build time-course wide matrix: mean expr per treatment × time point stroke$long$time_group = paste0(stroke$long$treatment, "_D", stroke$long$conc)  # Mean expression per protein × time_group stroke_means = aggregate(   expr ~ UniqueID + time_group,   data = stroke$long[stroke$long$treatment == "StrkIp", ],  # stroke model   FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE )  # Reshape to wide stroke_wide = reshape2::dcast(stroke_means, UniqueID ~ time_group, value.var = "expr") rownames(stroke_wide) = stroke_wide$UniqueID stroke_wide$UniqueID = NULL  # Keep top 500 most variable proteins vars = apply(stroke_wide, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE) stroke_wide_top = stroke_wide[names(sort(vars, decreasing = TRUE)[1:500]), ] stroke_wide_top[is.na(stroke_wide_top)] = 0  cat(sprintf("Time-course matrix: %d proteins × %d time points\n",             nrow(stroke_wide_top), ncol(stroke_wide_top))) #> Time-course matrix: 500 proteins × 5 time points colnames(stroke_wide_top) #> [1] "StrkIp_D1"  "StrkIp_D14" "StrkIp_D28" "StrkIp_D3"  "StrkIp_D7" clitheme("broadsheet") #> Theme set to: broadsheet cliplot(stroke_wide_top,         type = type_pattern(           k           = 6,           method      = "kmeans",           ncol        = 3,           line_alpha  = 0.3,           centroid_color = "#E64B35"         ),         stat.test = NULL,         title    = "**Figure 7** — Stroke Time-Course Pattern Clustering",         subtitle = "K-means (k=6) of 500 most variable proteins across 5 time points") +   cli_markdown()

text: Rank-abundance curve stroke brain proteomics — standard QC plot showing dynamic range protein detection:
code: # Aggregate mean expression per protein stroke_expr = aggregate(expr ~ UniqueID, data = stroke$long, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) names(stroke_expr) = c("Protein", "Intensity")  # Sort by intensity descending stroke_expr = stroke_expr[order(-stroke_expr$Intensity), ] stroke_expr$Rank = 1:nrow(stroke_expr)  # Highlight top 5 and some known proteins highlight_ids = stroke_expr$Protein[c(1, 10, 50, 200, 1000)]  cat(sprintf("Dynamic range: %.0f – %.0f (%.0f×)\n",             min(stroke_expr$Intensity), max(stroke_expr$Intensity),             max(stroke_expr$Intensity) / min(stroke_expr$Intensity))) #> Dynamic range: 222 – 17217332 (77423×) clitheme("science") #> Theme set to: science cliplot(Intensity ~ Rank, data = stroke_expr,         type = type_rankabundance(           log_scale      = "10",           point_color    = "#4DBBD5",           marginal_type  = "density",           label_genes    = highlight_ids,           label_color    = "#E64B35",           label_size     = 3         ),         stat.test = NULL,         title    = "**Figure 8** — Rank-Abundance Curve (Stroke Brain Proteomics)",         subtitle = sprintf("log₁₀ intensity | %d proteins detected", nrow(stroke_expr)),         caption  = sprintf("Dynamic range: %.0f× | Top 5 proteins highlighted",                           max(stroke_expr$Intensity)/min(stroke_expr$Intensity))) +   cli_markdown()

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: Compare fold-changes two AD/PD contrasts: AD vs. Control PD vs. Control. reveals proteins consistently differentially regulated across two related diseases:  strong positive correlation indicates AD PD share many dysregulated proteins cortex, disease-specific outliers visible -diagonal quadrants.
code: # Extract two comparisons and build standard-format data frames ad_vs_ctl = subset(adpd$results, test == "ADvsCTL")[, c("UniqueID", "logFC", "P.Value")] pd_vs_ctl = subset(adpd$results, test == "PDvsCTL")[, c("UniqueID", "logFC", "P.Value")]  # Rename to standard column names expected by type_deg_compare deg1 = ad_vs_ctl  # Column "logFC" will be used as comp1 logFC deg2 = pd_vs_ctl  # Column "logFC" will be used as comp2 logFC  # Merge on UniqueID deg_merged = merge(deg1, deg2, by = "UniqueID", suffixes = c("_AD", "_PD")) # After merge: logFC_AD = comp1 logFC, logFC_PD = comp2 logFC  # For type_deg_compare, rename comp2's logFC column deg2_clean = deg2 names(deg2_clean)[names(deg2_clean) == "logFC"] = "logFC_comp2"  # Label top concordant hits deg_merged$effect = abs(deg_merged$logFC_AD) + abs(deg_merged$logFC_PD) top_labels = head(deg_merged[order(-deg_merged$effect), ], 12)$UniqueID  cat(sprintf("Merged proteins: %d\n", nrow(deg_merged))) #> Merged proteins: 7163 cat(sprintf("Concordant direction: %.1f%%\n",             100 * sum(sign(deg_merged$logFC_AD) == sign(deg_merged$logFC_PD), na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(deg_merged))) #> Concordant direction: 58.7% clitheme("cell") #> Theme set to: cell cliplot(logFC_AD ~ UniqueID, data = deg_merged,         type = type_deg_compare(           comp2_data  = deg2_clean,           merge_by    = "UniqueID",           add_lm      = TRUE,           label_genes = top_labels,           same_scale  = TRUE         ),         stat.test = NULL,         title    = "**Figure 9** — Cross-Disease DEG Comparison",         subtitle = "log₂FC: AD vs. Control × PD vs. Control (cortex proteomics)",         xlab     = "log₂FC (PD vs. Control)",         ylab     = "log₂FC (AD vs. Control)") +   cli_markdown() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

title: Translational Proteomics and Functional Pathway Enrichment
text: pathway-inspired bubble heatmap showing top DE proteins across six AD/PD comparisons:
code: # Select top DE proteins from each comparison top_per_test = lapply(unique(adpd$results$test), function(tst) {   sub = subset(adpd$results, test == tst)   sub = sub[order(sub$P.Value), ]   head(sub$UniqueID, 6) }) top_all = unique(unlist(top_per_test))  # Build bubble heatmap data bh_rows = expand.grid(   Protein = top_all,   Comparison = unique(adpd$results$test),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  bh_rows$logFC = sapply(1:nrow(bh_rows), function(i) {   row = subset(adpd$results,                UniqueID == bh_rows$Protein[i] & test == bh_rows$Comparison[i])   if (nrow(row) > 0) row$logFC[1] else NA }) bh_rows$PValue = sapply(1:nrow(bh_rows), function(i) {   row = subset(adpd$results,                UniqueID == bh_rows$Protein[i] & test == bh_rows$Comparison[i])   if (nrow(row) > 0) -log10(row$P.Value[1]) else NA })  bh_rows = bh_rows[!is.na(bh_rows$logFC), ] bh_rows$absFC = abs(bh_rows$logFC) bh_rows$Gene  = sub("_.*", "", bh_rows$Protein) cliplot(Gene ~ Comparison, data = bh_rows,         by = bh_rows$absFC,         type = type_bubble_heatmap(           label_threshold = 1.5,           max_size        = 8.5,           size_name       = "|log₂FC|",           fill_name       = expression(-log[10]~"P"),           fill_low        = "#4575B4",           fill_mid        = "#FFFFBF",           fill_high       = "#D73027"         ),         extra_data = list(fill = bh_rows$PValue),         stat.test  = NULL,         title      = "**Figure 10** — Diamond Bubble Heatmap",         subtitle   = "Top DE Proteins × AD/PD Comparisons (size = |log₂FC|, colour = significance)") +   cli_markdown()

title: Clinical Trials, Survival Analysis, and Oncology Trajectories

what: Figure 2: Multivariable Cox Regression Forest Plot
title: Clinical Trials, Survival Analysis, and Oncology Trajectories
text: Forest plots summarize multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Science Lancet style: - Alternating subtle row stripes (stripe = TRUE) guide reader’s eye across wide canvases. - Pooled summary estimates highlighted high-contrast diamond glyphs (diamond = TRUE). - Odds/Hazard ratio estimates 95% CIs aligned cleanly along vertical axis.
code: # Fit Cox proportional hazards model cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog + wt.loss, data = lung) cox_sum <- summary(cox_fit)  # Prepare forest plot data frame forest_df <- data.frame(   Variable = c("Age (per year)", "Male vs. Female",                "ECOG PS (per point)", "Weight loss (per lb)"),   HR       = cox_sum$conf.int[, "exp(coef)"],   CI_low   = cox_sum$conf.int[, "lower .95"],   CI_high  = cox_sum$conf.int[, "upper .95"],   P        = cox_sum$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"] )  clitheme("science")  cliplot(HR ~ Variable, data = forest_df,         type = type_forest(           ref_line    = TRUE,           sort        = TRUE,           point_size  = 4,           ci_width    = 1.2,           stripe      = TRUE,           show_values = TRUE,           sig_color   = "#E64B35",           ns_color    = "#3C5488"         ),         title    = "**Figure 2** — Multivariable Cox Proportional Hazards Model",         subtitle = "Overall Survival Hazard Ratios (95% CI) with Row Stripes",         caption  = "NCCTG Advanced Lung Cancer (n = 228)") +   cli_markdown()

text: solid tumor trials, waterfall plot displays maximum percent change target lesion diameter relative baseline individual patient. Standard RECIST v1.1 response cutoffs (+20% Progressive Disease, -30% Partial Response) indicated dashed threshold lines:
code: set.seed(42) n_pts <- 30  imtrial <- data.frame(   Patient    = paste0("PT-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_pts)),   BestChange = sort(rnorm(n_pts, mean = -22, sd = 32)),   BestResp   = sample(c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD"), n_pts,                       replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.10, 0.30, 0.35, 0.25)),   Duration   = pmax(2, round(rnorm(n_pts, mean = 16, sd = 7), 1)),   Ongoing    = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n_pts, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.4, 0.6)) )  clitheme("broadsheet")  cliplot(BestChange ~ Patient, data = imtrial,         type = type_waterfall(           show_labels = FALSE,           n_skip_label = 1,           bar_width   = 0.72,           response_thresholds = c("PD" = 20, "PR" = -30)         ),         title    = "**Figure 3A** — Best Tumor Response from Baseline (Waterfall)",         subtitle = "RECIST v1.1 Thresholds: PD (+20%) and PR (-30%)",         ylab     = "Best % Change in Target Lesions",         legend   = "bottom") +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6.5)) +   cli_markdown()

what: Figure 3B: Swimmer Plot with Ongoing Indicators & RECIST Events
title: Clinical Trials, Survival Analysis, and Oncology Trajectories
text: Following Clinical Archetype 13, swimmer plots track patient treatment timelines. Patients actively continuing therapy database lock distinguished arrowheads bar tips (ongoing = "Ongoing"), key clinical events overlaid RECIST glyphs:
code: set.seed(123) n_events_per_pt <- sample(1:3, n_pts, replace = TRUE) events_list <- lapply(seq_len(n_pts), function(i) {   n_ev <- n_events_per_pt[i]   dur  <- imtrial$Duration[i]   times <- sort(round(runif(n_ev, min = 0.5, max = pmax(1.0, dur - 0.8)), 1))   ev_types <- sample(c("Progression", "AE", "Dose Reduction", "Response", "Surgery"),                      n_ev, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.10))   data.frame(ID = imtrial$Patient[i], Time = times, Event = ev_types) }) events_df <- do.call(rbind, events_list)  clitheme("cell")  cliplot(Duration ~ Patient, data = imtrial,         type = type_swimmer(           bar_fill      = "BestResp",           ongoing       = "Ongoing",           event_times   = events_df,           show_duration = TRUE,           bar_alpha     = 0.85,           bar_linewidth = 4.0         ),         bar_palette = "jama",         title   = "**Figure 3B** — Patient Treatment Trajectories (Swimmer)",         subtitle = "Arrows indicate ongoing therapy at data lock | Overlay: RECIST Events",         xlab    = "",         ylab    = "Time on Study (months)",         legend  = "bottom") +   theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)) +   cli_markdown()

what: Figure 5: Longitudinal Trajectories with Clinical Severity Bands
title: Clinical Trials, Survival Analysis, and Oncology Trajectories
text: Patient biomarkers clinical scores exhibit substantial -subject variability. Longitudinal Trajectory Plot (Clinical Archetype 4) overlays semi-transparent individual patient profiles onto shaded reference severity bands (e.g., Mild, Moderate, Severe), anchored bold group mean ribbon sample size callouts (n=…n = \dots):
code: set.seed(42) n_patients = 20 visits = c("Baseline", "Cycle 2", "Cycle 4", "Cycle 6", "Follow-up") traj_df = expand.grid(Patient = paste0("PT-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_patients)), Visit = visits)  # Simulate circulating biomarker decline under effective targeted therapy base_vals = rep(runif(n_patients, 55, 90), each = length(visits)) decay_vals = rep(c(0, 15, 32, 48, 55), times = n_patients) noise = rnorm(nrow(traj_df), mean = 0, sd = 5) traj_df$Marker = pmax(2, pmin(100, base_vals - decay_vals + noise))  clitheme("science")  cliplot(Marker ~ Visit | Patient, data = traj_df,         type = type_trajectory(           severity_bands  = list(Normal = c(0, 25), Elevated = c(25, 50), Critical = c(50, 100)),           severity_colors = c(Normal = "#E8F8F5", Elevated = "#FEF9E7", Critical = "#FADBD8"),           show_mean       = TRUE,           show_ci         = TRUE,           show_n          = TRUE         ),         title    = "**Figure 5** — Longitudinal Biomarker Response Trajectories",         subtitle = "Circulating Tumor Protein Dynamics with Severity Stratification",         ylab     = "Tumor Biomarker Concentration (ng/mL)") +   theme(plot.margin = margin(5.5, 22, 5.5, 5.5, "pt")) +   cli_markdown()

code: # Helper to resolve bundled package data resolve_data = function(filename) {   pkg_path = system.file("extdata", filename, package = "cliomicplot")   if (pkg_path != "" && file.exists(pkg_path)) return(pkg_path)   fallback = file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback)) return(fallback)   fallback2 = file.path("inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback2)) return(fallback2)   stop("Cannot find data file: ", filename) }  # Load stroke time-course proteomics stroke_env = new.env() load(resolve_data("StrokeBrain_TimeCourse.RData"), envir = stroke_env)  # Merge gene symbols stroke_long = merge(stroke_env$data_long,                     stroke_env$ProteinGeneName[, c("UniqueID", "Gene.Name")],                     by = "UniqueID", all.x = TRUE)  # Select Mpeg1 (macrophage/microglia activation marker) and identify individual replicates mpeg1 = subset(stroke_long, Gene.Name == "Mpeg1") mpeg1$Day = as.numeric(mpeg1$conc) mpeg1$Treatment = mpeg1$treatment mpeg1 = mpeg1[order(mpeg1$Treatment, mpeg1$Day, mpeg1$sampleid), ] mpeg1$Individual = paste0(mpeg1$Treatment, "_Mouse", ave(seq_len(nrow(mpeg1)), mpeg1$Treatment, mpeg1$Day, FUN = seq_along))  clitheme("science")  cliplot(expr ~ Day | Treatment, data = mpeg1,         group   = "Individual",         type    = type_lines(linewidth = 1.1, add_points = TRUE, point_size = 2.2),         palette = "jco",         title   = "**Figure 6A** — Mpeg1 Macrophage Marker Time Course",         subtitle = "Stroke Brain Proteomics — Individual Mouse Replicate Trajectories (Days 1–28)",         xlab    = "Days Post-Onset",         ylab    = "Protein Expression (LFQ Intensity)") +   cli_markdown()

X-linked transcriptome dysregulation across immune cells systemic lupus erythematosus. Biology Sex Differences. 2025;16(1):69. what: Figure 1 - X-linked transcriptome dysregulation across immune cells
title: Recreating a Published Figure: SLE X-Chromosome Dysregulation
text: paper’s Figure 1 shows X-linked transcription disturbed SLE. reproduce four panels: () distribution X/-ratio across 27 immune cell types (SLE vs HC), (b) volcano plots X-linked differential expression representative cells immune lineage, (c) mean-logFC heatmap consistently dysregulated X-linked genes per lineage, (d) Normalized Enrichment Score (NES) heatmap immune-related KEGG pathways ranked X/-ratio correlation. Recreated Figure 1 (SLE X-linked dysregulation). Panel : X/-ratio boxplots. Panel b: volcano small multiples representative cells. Panel c: mean logFC heatmap consistently dysregulated X-linked genes lineage. Panel d: KEGG NES heatmap. Panel grouped boxplot jittered points - one cliplot() call: Panel c aggregates per-cell-type DE results gene x lineage matrix mean logFC genes consistently (>= 80% cell types lineage) - -regulated, draws publication heatmap type_heatmap():
code: pat = load_sle("sle_patients.rda")$sle_patients pat$Cell_Type = factor(pat$Cell_Type,                        levels = c("CD16p_Mono", "CL_Mono", "Int_Mono",                                   "NC_Mono", "LDG", "Neu", "mDC", "pDC", ...)) pat$Condition = factor(pat$Condition, levels = c("SLE", "HC"))  cliplot(X_Ratio ~ Cell_Type | Condition, data = pat,         type = type_boxplot(add_jitter = TRUE, jitter_size = 0.55,                             jitter_alpha = 0.3, width = 0.65),         theme = "nature", palette = "nejm") +   labs(x = NULL, y = "X/A ratio") +   cli_panel_label("a") +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 6.5),         legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank()) de = load_sle("sle_xlinked_de.rda")$sle_xlinked_de de = de[de$Classification != "Non-significant", ] de$Lineage = lineage_map[as.character(de$Cell_Type)]   # lineage_map in script de$Up = de$Classification == "Up-regulated"  consistent_genes = lapply(unique(lineage_map), function(L) {   sub = de[de$Lineage == L, ]   n   = table(lineage_map)[[L]]   uc  = tapply(sub$Up, sub$Gene, sum)   dc  = tapply(sub$Up == FALSE, sub$Gene, sum)   mu  = tapply(sub$logFC[sub$Up], sub$Gene[sub$Up], mean)   md  = tapply(sub$logFC[!sub$Up], sub$Gene[!sub$Up], mean)   data.frame(Gene = c(names(uc)[uc >= 0.8 * n], names(dc)[dc >= 0.8 * n]),              Lineage = L,              logFC = c(mu[names(uc)[uc >= 0.8 * n]],                        md[names(dc)[dc >= 0.8 * n]]),              stringsAsFactors = FALSE) }) consistent_genes = do.call(rbind, consistent_genes)  mat = reshape2::acast(consistent_genes, Gene ~ Lineage, value.var = "logFC") mat[is.na(mat)] = 0  cliplot(mat, type = type_heatmap(scale = "none", cluster_rows = FALSE,                                  cluster_cols = FALSE, show_rownames = TRUE,                                  show_colnames = TRUE, legend_title = "mean logFC"),         theme = "nature")

what: Open Axes vs. Full-Box Frames: Which to Choose?
title: Themes and Palettes in cliomicplot
text: Nature Science strongly prefer removing top right spines maximize data ink avoid confining visual field. Outward tick marks prevent overlap data points near axis boundaries. Elsevier, IEEE, many specialized SCI journals require full rectangular frames enclosing four sides plot. theme_cli_scifig() applies 0.5 pt dark borders, crisp outward tick marks, 0.3 pt dashed reference grid lines.

title: Differential Expression Volcano Plots with GEO Datasets
text: dermatological transcriptomics translational medicine, differential expression studies rarely evaluate single comparison isolation. Instead, clinical investigations rely series contrasts: Disease Phenotyping Triad: Contrasting Atopic Dermatitis (AD) Psoriasis (PSO) Healthy Controls (HC), alongside direct head--head AD vs. PSO comparisons dissect Th2 versus Th17/Th22 immunophenotypic divergence. Therapeutic Resolution: Evaluating longitudinal cross-cohort treatment response across targeted biologics (e.g., Dupilumab anti-IL4Rα\alpha, tralokinumab anti-IL13, cerdulatinib dual SYK/JAK, SAR444727 RIPK1 inhibitor) track reversal disease-driving expression signatures. vignette demonstrates complete series volcano plots using real clinical transcriptomics NCBI GEO accession GSE121212 cross-cohort treatment meta-analyses. figures generated using type_volcano() cliplot().

title: Differential Expression Volcano Plots with GEO Datasets
text: analysis integrates four curated differential expression contrasts bundled directly cliomicplot: contrast table provides HGNC gene symbols effect estimates (log⁡2FC\log_2\text{FC}), standard errors (lfcSE), raw p-values, Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rates (padj).
code: # Helper to resolve bundled datasets resolve_data = function(filename) {   pkg_path = system.file("extdata", filename, package = "cliomicplot")   if (pkg_path != "" && file.exists(pkg_path)) return(pkg_path)   fallback = file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback)) return(fallback)   fallback2 = file.path("inst", "extdata", filename)   if (file.exists(fallback2)) return(fallback2)   stop("Cannot locate ", filename) }  series = readRDS(resolve_data("geo_dermatology_series_de.rds"))  # Inspect available contrasts names(series) #> [1] "ad_vs_hc"       "pso_vs_hc"      "ad_vs_pso"      "treatment_meta" #> [5] "series_tidy"

Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) Dumbbell (Archetype 1) # Compare observed effect sizes vs validated MCID threshold cliplot(Estimate ~ Endpoint, data = mcid_df,         type = type_mcid(mcid = "MCID", n_treated = "N"))  # 2. Longitudinal Trajectory with Clinical Severity Bands (Archetype 4) # Spaghetti paths + bold mixed-model mean + shaded Mild/Moderate/Severe bands cliplot(Score ~ Visit | Patient, data = longitudinal_df,         type = type_trajectory(show_mean = TRUE, show_n = TRUE))  # 3. Kaplan-Meier with Cumulative Incidence & Landmark Milestones (Archetype 5) # Zero external dependencies; exact percentages at 6mo, 1y, 2y callouts cliplot(Surv(time, status) ~ sex, data = lung,         type = type_km(cumulative_incidence = TRUE, milestones = c(180, 365, 730)))  # 4. Swimmer Plot with Ongoing Indicators (Archetype 13) # Ongoing therapy arrowheads at bar ends + RECIST event milestones cliplot(Duration ~ Patient, data = pt_data,         type = type_swimmer(bar_fill = "Response", ongoing = "Ongoing", event_times = events))  # 5. Forest Plot with Alternating Stripes & Pooled Diamonds (Archetype 9) # Subtle row striping eliminates eye drift across wide canvases cliplot(HR ~ Variable, data = meta_df,         type = type_forest(stripe = TRUE, diamond = TRUE, show_values = TRUE))

what: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
title: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
text: Calculates empirical statistical linkages connecting omics features network modules external clinical environmental indicators. resulting data frame directly feeds cliplot_env_network via links argument. Computes module eigengenes (centroid abundance profiles), runs bivariate correlation tests (Spearman Pearson) Mantel dissimilarity associations, applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) adjustments, selects statistically significant top-ranked linkages.

title: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
code: cli_calc_env_links(   comm_data,   env_data,   modules = NULL,   method = c("spearman", "pearson"),   fdr_cutoff = 0.05,   top_n = 5,   min_abs_r = 0.2,   module_summary = c("eigengene", "mean") )

title: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
text: comm_data Numeric matrix data frame omics/microbiome abundance (samples rows, features columns). env_data Numeric matrix, data frame, named list environmental/clinical indicators (samples rows, indicators columns). named list 1 4 matrices/data frames supplied, domain processed domain tag. modules Optional named character factor vector mapping feature IDs module names (e.g. c("Taxon_1" = "Mod_1", "Taxon_2" = "Mod_1")). NULL, features grouped modules automatically using hierarchical clustering, individual features tested directly. method Correlation metric: "spearman" (default, robust outliers) "pearson". fdr_cutoff Numeric significance threshold Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (default 0.05). NULL links meet threshold, top top_n links retained. top_n Optional integer specifying maximum number links retain per module environmental domain (default 5). min_abs_r Numeric minimum absolute correlation coefficient \(|r|\) required retain link (default 0.25). module_summary Summary method features within module: "eigengene" (first principal component, default) "mean" (standardized mean abundance).

title: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
text: data frame containing formatted link linkages columns: env Name environmental clinical indicator variable module Name target network module r Bivariate correlation coefficient p Raw asymptotic two-sided p-value fdr Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (q-value) log10p Negative log10 p-value (\(-\log_{10}(P)\)) sign Direction association: "Positive" "Negative" domain Domain name env_data supplied named list

title: Automated Calculation of Empirical Omics-to-Environment Links — cli_calc_env_links
code: set.seed(42) comm <- matrix(rpois(50 * 30, lambda = 15), nrow = 50, ncol = 30) colnames(comm) <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:30) env <- data.frame(   pH = rnorm(50, 6.5, 0.8),   Moisture = rnorm(50, 45, 10),   Temp = rnorm(50, 22, 4) ) mods <- setNames(paste0("Mod_", rep(1:3, each = 10)), colnames(comm)) links <- cli_calc_env_links(comm, env, modules = mods, method = "spearman") head(links) #>    env module          r          p          domain       fdr   log10p     sign #> 1 Temp  Mod_3 -0.2697239 0.05847339 External_Domain 0.5262605 1.233042 Negative

title: Permutation Significance Testing for Cross-Network Structural Differences — cli_network_permutation
text: comm_data Numeric matrix data frame feature abundances (samples rows, features columns). group Factor character vector specifying condition assignments sample. Must match nrow(comm_data) contain least 2 distinct groups. ref_group Optional character string designating baseline reference group. NULL, first level group used. test_group Optional character string designating comparison group. NULL, second level group used. cor_method Correlation metric: "spearman" (default) "pearson". cor_cutoff Absolute correlation threshold \(|r|\) establish network edges (default 0.35). p_cutoff Significance threshold correlation p-values (default 0.05). n_perm Integer. Number permutation iterations (default 199). seed Optional integer seed reproducibility.

title: Permutation Significance Testing for Cross-Network Structural Differences — cli_network_permutation
text: data frame summarizing observed metrics, permuted null means, standard errors,   two-sided permutation p-values: metric Topological network metric ref_val Observed metric value reference condition test_val Observed metric value test condition delta_obs Observed difference (test_val - ref_val) perm_mean Mean permuted null differences perm_se Standard error permuted null differences p_perm Two-sided empirical permutation p-value

title: Permutation Significance Testing for Cross-Network Structural Differences — cli_network_permutation
code: set.seed(42) comm <- matrix(rpois(40 * 25, lambda = 12), nrow = 40, ncol = 25) colnames(comm) <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:25) grp <- rep(c("Control", "Treatment"), each = 20) perm_res <- cli_network_permutation(comm, grp, n_perm = 49, seed = 42) print(perm_res) #>  #> ================================================================= #>  cliomicplot: Cross-Network Permutation Test #>  Reference (Control) vs Comparison (Treatment) #>  Number of Permutations: 49 #> ================================================================= #>                   metric ref_val test_val delta_obs perm_mean perm_se p_perm #>             Edge Density  0.0500   0.0500    0.0000   -0.0034  0.0228   1.00 #>     Natural Connectivity  0.5612   0.5761    0.0149   -0.0333  0.3004   0.96 #>  Negative/Positive Ratio  0.5000   0.5000    0.0000    0.0141  0.4859   1.00 #>              Mean Degree  1.2000   1.2000    0.0000   -0.0816  0.5461   1.00 #>   Clustering Coefficient  0.0000   0.0000    0.0000    0.0027  0.1197   1.00 #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>  Note: Two-sided empirical p-value: (1 + sum(|delta_null| >= |delta_obs|)) / (B + 1) #>

what: Simulate Multi-Network Robustness Under Random and Targeted Node Attacks — cli_network_robustness
title: Simulate Multi-Network Robustness Under Random and Targeted Node Attacks — cli_network_robustness
text: Simulates cascading collapse progressive degradation biological networks across conditions, treatments, cohorts (e.g. KO vs WT vs OE). Tests resilience : "random": Random species gene loss (simulated across Monte Carlo permutations). "degree": Targeted attacks removing highest-degree hub nodes first. "betweenness": Targeted attacks removing critical network bottleneck nodes first. Tracks remaining active node fraction, spectral natural connectivity, giant component size across progressive node removal fractions.

title: Simulate Multi-Network Robustness Under Random and Targeted Node Attacks — cli_network_robustness
text: networks Named list square numeric adjacency/correlation matrices, single numeric matrix. Names correspond condition/cohort labels (e.g. list(KO = mat1, WT = mat2)). attack Character vector specifying attack types: "random", "degree", /"betweenness". Default c("random", "degree"). rm_fractions Numeric vector node removal fractions 0.05 0.95 (default seq(0.05, 0.90, = 0.05)). metric Metric monitor: "natural_connectivity" (default), "remain_nodes" (fraction nodes least 1 edge), "giant_component" (relative size largest connected component). n_perm Integer. Number permutations random removal (default 30). threshold Numeric edge threshold binarize correlation matrices (default 0.3). seed Optional integer seed reproducibility.

title: Manhattan Plot for Genome-Wide and Microbial Association Studies — type_manhattan
text: Creates publication-ready Manhattan plots host GWAS microbial genome-wide association studies (mGWAS). title: Manhattan Plot for Genome-Wide and Microbial Association Studies — type_manhattan
text: threshold Significance cutoff. raw p-values q-values, defaults 0.05 (5e-8 genome-wide significance). data already -log10 scale, specifies vertical line position. is_already_log10 Logical. TRUE, y-axis values assumed already \(-\log_{10}(p)\) \(-\log_{10}(q)\). Default FALSE. point_size Size variant points (default 1.2). point_alpha Opacity variant points (default 0.85). chr_colors Character vector two alternating colors chromosomes (default c("#2B5C8F", "#82B0D2")). highlight_color Color variants exceeding significance threshold (default "#E64B35"). threshold_color Color horizontal significance line (default "#888888"). threshold_linetype Line type threshold line (default "dashed"). label_hits Logical. TRUE, annotates significant variants exceeding threshold text labels. Default TRUE. label_col Column name character vector containing variant gene labels. NULL, auto-detects columns named "label", "gene", "snp", "hit". max_overlaps Maximum overlapping labels allowed ggrepel (default 25). xlab Label x-axis. Defaults "Chromosome" multi-chromosome "Chromosome position (bp)" single-contig genomes. ylab Label y-axis (default expression(-log[10]~italic(p))).

title: Manhattan Plot for Genome-Wide and Microbial Association Studies — type_manhattan

what: Cis-pQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Heatmap — type_mr_coloc
title: Cis-pQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Heatmap — type_mr_coloc
text: Creates publication-ready Mendelian Randomization (MR) Bayesian colocalization heatmaps (Clinical Archetype 36) evaluating causal genetic links molecular exposures (e.g. plasma pQTLs, eQTLs, single-cell marker signatures) complex disease endpoints. Evaluates Wald ratio effect sizes (Z-score beta) diverging gradient, overlays odds ratios p < 0.05, outlines tiles passing multiple-testing thresholds (e.g. Bonferroni), places corner glyphs robust colocalization (PP.H4 >= 0.80), mutes discordant associations (PP.H3 >= 0.80, MHC/HLA linkage disequilibrium artifacts) italicized grey text.

title: Cis-pQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Heatmap — type_mr_coloc
code: type_mr_coloc(   beta_col = NULL,   se_col = NULL,   z_col = NULL,   p_col = NULL,   or_col = NULL,   pp4_col = NULL,   pp3_col = NULL,   fdr_col = NULL,   set_col = NULL,   family_col = NULL,   p_threshold = 0.05,   bonferroni = TRUE,   coloc_threshold = 0.8,   discordant_threshold = 0.8,   text_size = 2,   text_format = "%.2f",   glyph_shape = 17,   glyph_size = 1,   glyph_nudge = c(0.36, 0.3),   colors = c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"),   limits = c(-6, 6),   fill_name = "z of Wald ratio",   border_color = "grey85",   border_linewidth = 0.25,   frame_color = "black",   frame_linewidth = 0.55,   show_caption = TRUE,   caption = NULL,   xlab = NULL,   ylab = NULL )

title: Cis-pQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Heatmap — type_mr_coloc
text: beta_col Column name MR effect estimate (beta Wald ratio). se_col Column name standard error MR estimate. z_col Column name Z-score (beta / SE). Auto-computed beta_col se_col present. p_col Column name association p-value. or_col Column name odds ratio per SD (effect size text display). pp4_col Column name colocalization posterior probability hypothesis 4 (shared causal variant, \(\text{PP.H4}\)). pp3_col Column name colocalization posterior probability hypothesis 3 (distinct causal variants / LD artifact, \(\text{PP.H3}\)). fdr_col Column name FDR-adjusted q-value. set_col Column name exposure grouping (e.g. marker protein class: effector vs memory). family_col Column name outcome disease family (e.g. Cardiovascular, Allergic, Autoimmune). p_threshold Numeric p-value threshold displaying numerical effect sizes inside tiles (default 0.05). bonferroni Logical numeric. TRUE (default), computes 0.05 / N pairs draws prominent black border around significant tiles. numeric, uses specified threshold. Set FALSE disable. coloc_threshold Minimum PP.H4 display colocalization corner triangle glyph (default 0.80). discordant_threshold Minimum PP.H3 format text muted italic grey (default 0.80), flagging distinct variants locus. text_size Font size numbers inside tiles (default 2.0). text_format String format effect numbers (default "%.2f"). glyph_shape Point shape colocalization marker (default 17, solid triangle). glyph_size Size colocalization corner marker (default 1.0). glyph_nudge Numeric vector length 2 specifying x y nudge corner glyph (default c(0.36, 0.30)). colors Diverging color gradient vector length 3 (low, mid, high). Default c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"). limits Symmetrical color scale limits \(Z\)-score (default c(-6, 6)). Values beyond squished. fill_name Legend title color gradient (default "z Wald ratio"). border_color Grid border color tiles (default "grey85"). border_linewidth Grid line width tiles (default 0.25). frame_color Outline color Bonferroni-significant tiles (default "black"). frame_linewidth Outline stroke width Bonferroni-significant tiles (default 0.55). show_caption Logical. TRUE (default), appends standardized publication caption explaining numbers, frames, triangles, italicized text. caption Optional override caption string. xlab, ylab Axis labels.

title: cliomicplot 0.1.5
text: Microbial GWAS & Genomics Manhattan Plot (type_manhattan(), Archetype 27): Dedicated Manhattan plot builder supporting multi-chromosome host GWAS (natural chromosome ordering, centered x-axis labels, alternating hues) single-contig microbial GWAS (mGWAS). Includes significance cutoff line, hit highlighting threshold, automatic non-overlapping variant labeling via ggrepel. Differential Abundance Bubble Matrix (type_bubble_matrix(), Archetype 29): Two-dimensional dot plot encoding directional effect size (signed log⁡2FC\log_2\text{FC} regression coefficient) zero-centered diverging color gradient, significance (−log⁡10q-\log_{10} q) point radius across multiple anatomical sites, conditions, clinical visits. Longitudinal Transmission & Dyad Sharing Heatmap (type_sharing_heatmap(), Archetype 28): Discrete matrix visualization bacterial vertical transmission across mother-infant dyads strain persistence study visits (e.g. baseline infancy T1 versus 12 months T3). New Clinical Metagenomics Vignette (vignette("microbiome-mgwas")): Demonstrates end--end clinical metagenomics mGWAS workflows based VITALITY infant cohort: host FLG genetics vs SCORAD severity, differential abundance bubble matrix across anatomical sites, bacterial mGWAS Manhattan plot, dyad strain transmission. Documentation & Assets: Cleaned encoding artifacts across documentation, added new figure panels reference galleries, updated deployment configuration prevent broken image paths GitHub Pages.

title: cliomicplot 0.1.4
text: Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) Dumbbell Plot (type_mcid(), Archetype 1): Distinguish genuine clinical relevance large-cohort nominal significance (P<0.001P < 0.001). Connects observed treatment effect sizes validated instrument MCID thresholds (e.g. DLQI = 4.0, EASI = 6.6), point glyphs scaled sample size (NtreatedN_{\text{treated}}) endpoints ordered effect--MCID ratio. Longitudinal Clinical Trajectories Severity Bands (type_trajectory(), Archetype 4): Visualizes patient-level clinical heterogeneity without spaghetti hairballs. Overlays semi-transparent individual trajectories onto shaded background clinical severity bands (Mild, Moderate, Severe), anchored bold group mean trajectory confidence ribbon (95%95\% CI / SE) visit sample-size annotations (n=…n = \dots). Zero-Dependency Native KM & Cumulative Incidence (type_km(), Archetype 5): Completely removed hard dependency survminer. Driven native ggplot2 + survival engine supporting cumulative incidence ([1−S(t)]×100%[1 - S(t)] \times 100\%), landmark milestone callouts (milestones = c(...)) exact percentages directly curve, aligned numbers--risk tables, median survival crosshairs, log-rank pp-values. Clinical Oncology Swimmer Plot Enhancements (type_swimmer(), Archetype 13): Added ongoing therapy indicator rendering arrowheads ends timeline bars patients remaining therapy database lock. Unified clinical event shape/color contracts added duration annotations. Publication Forest Plot Enhancements (type_forest(), Archetype 9): Added alternating background row shading stripes (stripe = TRUE) eliminate horizontal eye drift across wide canvases, unclipped confidence interval labels, zero-magnitude negative sign suppression (-0.00 rounded 0.00), meta-analysis pooled summary diamonds (diamond = TRUE). SCI Full-Box Theme (theme_cli_scifig(), clitheme("scifig")): New publication theme adhering SCI / Elsevier / IEEE journal visual requirements: 4 visible black spines, outward-facing tick marks, subtle dashed reference grid. Expanded Publisher Presets & Compliance Checks (cli_journal_size(), cli_save()): Expanded 9 verified publisher presets (Nature, Nature Communications, Science, Cell, JAMA, NEJM, Lancet, PLOS, IEEE). Added arithmetic printable height verification, support numeric columns (1, 1.5, 2), submission format guidance (warning raster PNG supplied Nature/Science final manuscripts). Exported Standalone Theme Functions: Exported first-class ggplot2 themes theme_cli_nature(), theme_cli_science(), theme_cli_cell(), theme_cli_nejm(), theme_cli_lancet(), theme_cli_scifig(), theme_cli_bw(), theme_cli_classic(), theme_cli_minimal(), theme_cli_dark(), theme_cli_showcase(), theme_cli_broadsheet().
